title: Nemotron 3 Nano: many tasks crash in <3 seconds
description: In CRUSH + Nemotron Nano local run, 7 tasks crashed in 1-2s (both trials): collab-server, fts-search, monorepo-disaster, phantom-invoice, plugin-marketplace, task-queue, time-tracker. Scored workspace baselines, not real attempts. Check if llama.cpp connection issue (haight:8090), CRUSH startup failure, or model-rewrite hack fragility.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
Root cause: transient infrastructure issue + minor URL bug.

**Findings:**
- 14/32 trials crashed (all from one run). Second run of same tasks worked fine.
- Crashed tasks completed in 1-2s with 'No providers configured' error
- The proxy (openai_proxy.py) crashes immediately when haight:8090 is unreachable, so crush starts without a working provider
- Other haight-based adapters (crush-qwen3coder-local, crush-gemma4-local) show 1-5% crash rate -- same transient issue, less severe
- Tasks within the same run have mixed results (7 crashed, 12 ran normally), suggesting haight came back up partway through

**Fixes applied:**
- Added missing /v1 to upstream URL (http://haight:8090 -> http://haight:8090/v1) -- matches all other working haight adapters

**Not fixed (low priority):**
- No upstream connectivity check before crush starts -- proxy /health only checks proxy is listening, not that upstream is reachable
- No retry on proxy startup failure -- would help with transient haight outages

title: Zen meditation: ambiguity/hard regression (-8pp)
description: Meditate primitive regressed ambiguity/hard from 0.68 (v2) to 0.60 (v3). Only category where meditation made things worse. Hypothesis: ambiguous requirements need aggressive exploration, not stillness. Meditation may make the model too accepting of its first interpretation. Examine v2 vs v3 output, consider whether MIRROR or INVERSION stratagems would help.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
Root cause: meditation reduces implementation completeness, not understanding.

**Score breakdown (v2 -> v3):**
- hidden_tests: 0.212 -> 0.212 (identical)
- agent_tests: 1.0 -> 1.0 (identical)
- coverage: 0.938 -> 0.822 (-11.6pp)
- code_metrics: 1.0 -> 0.7 (-30pp)

**Interpretation:** The meditate primitive consumes context/turns on introspection that would otherwise go toward implementation. The model's understanding of the ambiguous spec isn't affected (same hidden_tests score), but it writes less complete code with worse metrics.

For ambiguity/hard tasks, the bottleneck is coverage and thoroughness, not insight. Meditation is counterproductive here because the task requires aggressive exploration and implementation, not stillness.

**Recommendation:** Task-specific stratagem routing (TD-h0r) should skip meditation for ambiguity tasks. MIRROR or INVERSION stratagems that encourage re-examining assumptions would be more appropriate.

title: Gemma 4 MoE: reasoning/hard bottleneck (0.20 across all 3 tasks)
description: Gemma 4 MoE hard benchmark: overall mean 0.398. Strengths: correctness 0.84, bugfix 0.75. Weakness: reasoning/hard 0.20 uniformly across all 3 tasks. Investigate whether model is giving up, going in circles, or confidently wrong. Compare with Sonnet/Opus reasoning scores. Determine if context window, instruction following, or raw reasoning limitation.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
Gemma 4 MoE uniformly fails reasoning/hard -- produces implementations that score 0.2 (workspace baseline: build/lint pass but zero hidden tests).

**Scores (9 trials across 3 tasks):**
- beam-splitter: 0.200, 0.200, 0.200 (Sonnet: 0.935-0.958)
- circuit-debugger: 0.200, 0.547, 0.200 (Sonnet: 0.787-0.827)
- factory-reset: 0.200, 0.323, 0.200 (Sonnet: 0.914-0.950)

Duration 300-600s per trial -- the model tries but produces wrong algorithms. This is a fundamental reasoning capability gap, not an instruction-following or context window issue. Gemma 4's strengths (correctness 0.84, bugfix 0.75) suggest it follows patterns well but can't discover novel algorithms.

No actionable fix beyond model improvement. This is a known capability boundary for this model class.

title: Greenfield/complex task 8: persistent 0.28 on Sonnet
description: One greenfield/complex task consistently scores 0.28 across all Sonnet variants (zen v1, v2, v3). Opus breaks through to 0.79. Need to examine the task description, check output JSONL for failure patterns, determine if this is a Sonnet capability ceiling or prompt/scaffolding issue.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
Root cause analysis complete. The persistent 0.28 composite is NOT a native module/infra bug.

**Findings:**
- hidden_tests=0.04 (1/25 pass) is from real implementation failures, not skipped tests
- Verified by running hidden tests in node:20 Docker container -- tests execute but fail on auth (401s), missing endpoints, etc.
- The task is bimodal across ALL models: implementations either get auth + API structure right (~1.0) or fail catastrophically (~0.04)
- Many Opus orchestrators also score 0.04 consistently (bmad, gsd, tango-and-cash, superpowers-plans)
- 386 trials analyzed: 52% score 1.0, 33% score 0.04, 15% in between

**The 0.28 composite formula:**
hidden_tests(0.04)*0.385 + agent_tests(~0)*0.308 + build_lint(1.0)*0.154 + code_metrics(0.7)*0.154 = 0.277

**Reclassification:** Not a Sonnet-specific capability ceiling. This is a high-variance task where the hidden test suite has a steep pass/fail cliff around auth implementation. The 1/25 test that passes is likely a test that doesn't require auth.

**Defensive fix applied:** Added install_cmd to T2, T7, T8, T10 in thunderdome.yaml to ensure native modules are rebuilt in validation containers. Won't affect scores but prevents potential future native module issues.

title: Experiment: task-specific stratagem routing
description: Zen helps greenfield (+57pp) and reasoning (+16pp) but hurts ambiguity (-8pp). Create a routing adapter that selects stratagem based on task category: ZEN for greenfield/reasoning, MIRROR or INVERSION for ambiguity, PIVOT for bugfix. Run full benchmark to compare against uniform zen (0.856) and baseline (0.866). Depends on understanding the ambiguity regression.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
## Results: metacog-routed-sonnet

**Overall: 87.4% @ $0.73/task** (38 trials, 19 tasks x 2, 97% pass rate)

### Suite Scores
- Standard (7 tasks): 96.6%
- Hard (12 tasks): 78.3%

### Comparison
| Orchestrator | Overall | Cost/task |
|---|---|---|
| v10 Haiku-routed | 90.2% | $1.20 |
| v8 combined Sonnet | 88.6% | $0.82 |
| v8 combined Opus | 88.6% | $1.45 |
| **metacog-routed-sonnet** | **87.4%** | **$0.73** |
| metacog-zen v3 Sonnet | 85.6% | ~$0.70 |

### Routing Analysis
Haiku classified 19 tasks into categories, routing to 4 of 5 possible stratagems:
- **fool**: 19 trials (50%) -- features, bugfix, recovery, algorithmic, default
- **veil**: 15 trials (39%) -- greenfield/complex (+ some misrouted)
- **drift**: 3 trials (8%) -- greenfield/simple
- **scrying**: 1 trial (3%) -- marathon (1 of 2 trials, other hit Haiku error)
- **mirror**: 0 trials -- never triggered (beam-splitter misclassified as greenfield)

### Routing Issues
1. **Haiku verbose responses** (3/38 trials): Haiku returned essay-length explanations instead of category labels. Wildcard matching in case statement still routed correctly by luck.
2. **Haiku classification errors**: beam-splitter (reasoning/hard) classified as GREENFIELD_COMPLEX/SIMPLE, reactive-spreadsheet (algorithmic/hard) classified as GREENFIELD_COMPLEX, financial-ledger (correctness/hard) classified as BUGFIX.
3. **Max turns error** (1/38): task-queue trial-1 Haiku hit max turns, fell back to default fool instead of scrying.

### Verdict
Stratagem routing on Sonnet scores 87.4%, slightly below v8 baseline (88.6%) but at lower cost ($0.73 vs $0.82). The routing adds Haiku classification overhead but doesn't clearly improve scores. Misclassification noise (beam-splitter, reactive-spreadsheet) prevents the intended mirror/fool stratagems from being tested properly. The Haiku verbose response issue suggests --max-turns 1 is unreliable for classification.

**Conclusion: Routing adds complexity without clear benefit over the base zen v3 approach (+1.8pp vs zen, -1.2pp vs v8 baseline).** The experiment does establish that metacog stratagems work on Sonnet (not just Opus where they were ablated), but per-category routing via Haiku is too noisy to outperform simpler approaches.

title: Scoring: pre-existing workspace code inflates crash scores
description: When adapters crash early (auth failure, 2s timeout), tasks still get scored against existing workspace. Examples: Opus bugfix/hard crashed 7s but scored 0.75; CRUSH+Nano tasks crashed 1-2s but scored 0.585-0.835. Proposal: flag crash scores separately, track workspace baseline vs agent contribution. Require minimum duration/token threshold (e.g. <10s or <100 tokens = score 0.0).

title: Marathon: Opus underperforms Sonnet (0.62 vs 0.76)
description: Zen v3 Opus scored 0.62 on marathon vs Sonnet's 0.76. Opus took 651s vs 451s. One of few categories where Opus does worse. Hypothesis: marathon rewards efficiency; Opus over-thinks, burning budget/time. Sonnet's direct approach may be an advantage. Single task category though, could be noise.

comments.author: Conclave Parallel Runner
comments.text:
Not a real pattern -- noise from single-trial zen data.

Across v8 methodology variants with 2+ trials each:
- Opus marathon mean: 0.652 (n=10)
- Sonnet marathon mean (comparable configs): 0.652 (n=11, excluding ralph/eval which often time out at 0.2)

The zen-specific gap (Opus 0.62 vs Sonnet 0.76) is a single-trial comparison on a single task. Not statistically meaningful. Opus does not systematically underperform on marathon.
